newsitem.title: USA: Accounting standards need to be modernized-GAO.
newsitem.headline: Accounting standards need to be modernized-GAO.

text.p: Accounting standards that dictate the information companies must provide to investors are falling out of step with the modern economy, the U.S. General Accounting Office said in a report released Tuesday.
Changes in the economy "are significantly challenging the relevance of historical cost-based financial statements and the traditional audit of those statements," the research arm of Congress said.

In the new economy, investors receive information more rapidly than in the past using online services, while companies fund their operations with complex financial instruments that can dramatically fluctuate in value, the GAO reported.
Under existing rules, companies often report the initial or historic cost of their assets instead of current values.

"For the accounting profession to successfully move to a more modern era of auditing and provide expanded assurance services, it must more vigorously continue to address the major unresolved issues," the GAO said.

The Financial Accounting Standards Board, a private body that sets accounting standards for public companies, has proposed new rules for complex instruments like derivatives. But companies have complained that the rules are burdensome and likely to confuse rather than edify investors.
The GAO called on the Securities and Exchange Commission to take the lead in forging a consensus among all parties to modernise accounting standards.
"The SEC, given its responsibilities under federal securities laws, is in a pivotal position to assume a leadership role," the GAO said.
The accounting profession could also do more to reveal fraudulent activity and prevent unexpected losses, the GAO found.
Auditors should review the effectiveness of companies' internal controls, the checks and balances put in place to prevent fraudulent or unauthorised transactions, the GAO said.

"Effective internal controls are the first line of defence for safeguarding assets and preventing fraudulent financial reporting -- a lesson well learned from the savings and loan crisis," the GAO said.

The GAO praised a recent SEC initiative to increase public participation in the accounting standards setting process. At the SEC's behest, the parent body of the FASB will include more public representatives.

The GAO report, titled "The Accounting Profession, Major Issues: Progress and Concerns," was prompted by a request from Congressman John Dingell, ranking minority member of the House Commerce Committee.
